name: In-car / "yapper" confession talking head
length: 20-60s, 1080x1920, one continuous take with jump cuts

shots.visual: Creator in a parked car, phone on dash mount at eye level, daylight from the windscreen
shots.audio_text: "I couldn't even wait to get inside to tell you this."

shots.visual: Same framing, jump cuts every 3-6s to remove pauses
shots.audio_text: Fast, personal story with one specific detail per line

shots.visual: She shows the product to camera (pulls necklace out of her collar)
shots.audio_text: Proof: "I've worn this in the ocean all week"

prompts.prompt: iPhone front camera, 1080p 30fps, phone mount on the dash, engine off, windows closed for clean audio, face lit by daylight (park facing the sun).

paid_ads.title: Luxmend: Test-it-live yapper ("we're gonna see if this actually works")
paid_ads.what: A woman talks to her front camera for 118 s while testing a split-end trimmer on her own hair, in one take with no cuts: "we're gonna see if this split end trimmer actually works… I'm not gonna cut the video at all."
paid_ads.how: Phone on a stand at eye level, natural light, one continuous take. Say the doubt first, then do the test on camera and react honestly. Product name only after the result.

paid_ads.title: Kristina's Fashion Essentials: "I'll be so disappointed if this doesn't work" lash-test yapper
paid_ads.what: A close-up selfie: "I'm gonna be so disappointed if this does not work exactly like everyone says it does… these lashes are seriously just so stubborn". She applies the mascara live and reacts. 106 s.
paid_ads.how: Name your specific problem ("straight Asian lashes"), say what you've heard, test it live, react. Keep the camera on your face and the problem area.

paid_ads.title: BioRoot Labs: Ingredient-nerd yapper (turmeric percentages)
paid_ads.what: A creator in a branded tee explains why she picked BioRoot: "95% curcumin, around 30 times more than the store bought" and black pepper "which majority of store bought ones don't have". 125 s; the brand has 1,000 active ads.
paid_ads.how: A creator holds the bottle and reads 2-3 numbers off the label, compares them with a generic store version, then gives her personal routine.

paid_ads.title: HappySupp: Girlfriend-voice men's multivitamin (HappySupp)
paid_ads.what: A woman in a black top to camera: "Cause ain't no way he taking this without me around… this is only for you and your girl. Don't get too crazy with it. This is the men's multivitamin by HappySupp… herbal blend to support your prostate." 86 s.
paid_ads.how: A female partner speaks to men about the product's effect on "him", in a playful tone.

paid_ads.title: Nothora: In-car storytime yapper (gossip hook)
paid_ads.what: A creator in the driver's seat tells a work-drama story ("I just got fired… because I told this woman…"), and the product drops in late. 94 s.
paid_ads.how: Parked car, seatbelt on, phone on the dash. Open with a 1-line drama, tell it for 40-60 s, then pivot: "anyway, the thing that got me through it…".

paid_ads.title: Feel Mighty: "Car chats" one-month update yapper (gifted, then hooked)
paid_ads.what: "Welcome to a new episode of car chats… I have been taking the mighty mushroom gummies for over a month now… initially these were sent to me as PR." 103 s.
paid_ads.how: A recurring creator series name, a dated update ("over a month now"), disclosure of gifting, and what changed.

paid_ads.title: Mariella Gut Health Expert: "Gross embarrassing story time" gut yapper (Mariella Gut Health Expert)
paid_ads.what: A creator on a couch: "Alright, gross embarrassing story time! A few months ago I started noticing that my smells were… terrible… I was feeling bloated, icky… I consulted a few physicians, they said something was wrong with my gut health…" 105 s.
paid_ads.how: Couch, casual, pyjama energy. Say "gross/embarrassing" in the first 2 s, give 2-3 specific symptoms in their own words, what they tried, the doctor moment, then the product.

qa_checklist: Hook lands in the first 1.5 s (video) or is readable at thumbnail size (static / slide 1).
Removal test: delete the product from the script. If it still makes sense, rewrite so the product is the payoff.
Matches the reference structure (same beat order and length band) before any creative twist.
Uses only real product imagery for the product; AI is for backgrounds, characters or b-roll, and is disclosed where required.
Every claim is on the brand's approved-claims list (PDP); no invented stats, reviews, doctors or customers.
Captions burned in and inside the safe zone; sound-off still understandable.
One clear CTA that matches the landing page offer.
Three hook variants delivered for the same body (test hooks, not whole new ads).
Avoid: Never film while driving; parked only.
Avoid: Over-scripted lines kill the "yapper" feel; give the creator bullet points, not a script.
Avoid: Disclose paid partnerships (#ad / Paid partnership label).
inputs: BRAND (name, product, price, offer, audience, proof points, banned claims)
ASSETS (real product photos/video, logo, fonts, colors)
outputs: brands/<brand-slug>.md with 3 concepts in the output schema below
per concept: script/slide copy, shot list, on-screen text, caption, CTA, 3 hook variants, prompts used
